query: Refractory high-entropy alloys are promising structural materials, but achieving a strong combination of strength and plasticity remains important. What single intervention could improve this strength–plasticity combination? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, its expected mechanism, the predicted improvement relative to an appropriate reference alloy, the conditions under which it should hold, supporting evidence from prior studies, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of a specific refractory element can improve the strength-plasticity combination in high-entropy alloys.
generation.intervention: Addition of a refractory element (e.g., Hf or Zr) to the alloy composition
generation.conditions: The alloy is processed under standard conditions (e.g., arc melting and drop casting) and tested at room temperature
generation.mechanism: The added refractory element enhances lattice distortion, leading to improved strength, while atomic-scale segregation promotes plasticity
generation.predicted_outcome: A 20% increase in yield strength and a 15% increase in ductility compared to the reference alloy
generation.baseline: A refractory high-entropy alloy without the added refractory element (e.g., AlCoCrFeNi)
generation.boundary: The alloy composition and processing conditions
generation.uncertainty: The optimal amount and type of refractory element to add, as well as the potential effects of other alloying elements

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of alloys: one with the added refractory element and one without. Test their mechanical properties (yield strength and ductility) using standard methods (e.g., uniaxial tensile testing).
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the alloy with the added refractory element does not show a significant improvement in strength-plasticity combination (i.e., <10% increase in yield strength or <5% increase in ductility) compared to the reference alloy, the hypothesis is falsified.
